matchups.recap: Arben got absolutely skull-fucked this week, dropping 113.6 points like it was a participation trophy while Rob served up 131.3 points of pure fantasy dominance. That 17.7-point margin is what happens when you build a roster with all the strategic vision of a blindfolded monkey throwing darts at a waiver wire. Arben's team looked like it was actively trying to tank, and congratulations—mission fucking accomplished.

Flamur got absolutely dick-slapped by 18.5 points this week, which is what happens when your "strategy" is apparently just praying that last year's waiver-wire scraps suddenly turn into league winners. You rolled out a roster that looked like it was assembled at a gas station at 11:59 PM on draft day, and Nori punished you like the fantasy football gods intended—watch next week's waiver wire like your season depends on it, because at this rate it absolutely does.

Ben got absolutely obliterated by 69.3 points—which is fitting because that's exactly how many brain cells he used when he built this dumpster fire of a roster. His team scored 78.7 points like it was playing in a flag football league for geriatrics, while Rinor put up nearly double that without breaking a sweat. Ben, buddy, I've seen better lineups from a guy drafting with a concussion and his eyes closed. Next week try actually starting players who are actively playing instead of whatever corpses you're rostering.

Veton got absolutely cock-blocked by 3 fucking points—close enough to taste victory, far enough to choke on it. Adam's team showed up to work while Veton's played like they were running their routes in quicksand, leaving just enough points on the bench to haunt him for the next three weeks. That's the kind of loss that makes you stare at your lineup at 2 AM wondering which of your draft picks personally wronged you. Better luck next week, chief—you're gonna need it.

Rilind got absolutely buttfucked by 25.3 points this week, which is fitting since his roster looked like it was assembled by someone playing fantasy football while blindfolded in a tornado. Dude's out here scoring 80 points like it's a participation trophy, while Faton was actually showing up with a functioning team that knew how to put points on the board. This wasn't even close—it was a full-blown ass-whipping that Rilind's going to feel for the next three weeks.

Ilir, you got absolutely dicked down by your own family—losing by 1.3 points is the fantasy equivalent of showing up to Thanksgiving knowing you're about to hear about this all goddamn year. Jetmir and Peter are gonna be running this in your face at every family dinner for the next twelve months, and honestly, you deserve it for putting together a roster so limp it couldn't score 95 points even when it mattered most. Next time maybe don't choke this hard when the family name's actually on the line—at least then you could look your relatives in the eye without flinching.

matchups.preview: Rob's season is already circling the drain at 1-4, and now he's gotta face the league's hottest team? This is gonna be a mercy killing. Nori's rolling with actual competent roster management while Rob's still trying to figure out why his draft-day reaches aren't panning out, and we're all about to watch it play out in real time this week.

Ben's 2-3 record is basically a participation trophy at this point—he's been treading water while Arben's actually out here winning games like a competent human. This week Ben gets to watch from the kiddie table as Arben's 4-1 juggernaut reminds him what it looks like when you don't panic-trade away your depth in Week 2. Ben's going to need a miracle and a refund on whatever draft advice he paid for.

Veton's bringing a 0-5 dumpster fire to face the only competent team in this league—Flamur's sitting pretty at 4-1 and about to remind everyone why Veton's been collecting Ls like they're going out of style. This matchup isn't a game, it's a mercy killing; Flamur's just gonna twist the knife one more time and send Veton home to cry into whatever waiver wire corpses he's been desperately plugging into his lineup.

Muriqi's sitting pretty at 3-2, but that's what happens when you've been coasting on bye weeks and cupcake matchups—time to face a real team and watch that record crumble like your draft strategy. Ahmetaj's 3-2 too, but at least he didn't luck his way there; this week he finally gets to punish Muriqi for whatever waiver-wire desperation moves got him this far.

Ilir rolls in sitting pretty at 3-2, but let's not pretend this isn't the week his house of cards comes crashing down against Adam's hungry 2-3 squad that's got nothing to lose. Adam's been quietly stockpiling waiver pickups while Ilir's coasting on fumes, and karma's about to bitch-slap that smug 3-win record right back down to earth. This is the upset everyone's been waiting for—Adam's about to remind Ilir why you can't just sleepwalk through the middle of the season.

Jetmir's cruising at 3-2 while Rilind's out here looking like he drafted exclusively based on vibes and a broken crystal ball at 1-4—this matchup's basically asking which team wants to stay relevant or if Rilind's ready to complete his descent into total irrelevance. Jetmir should be licking his chops facing a dumpster fire with wheels, but knowing this league's ability to find new ways to fail spectacularly, there's probably a 40% chance he manages to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory anyway.
